document: How CI executes the M5 conformance campaign
note: This contract is the canonical execution description beside the campaign script. The dedicated workflow is a thin provisioning and call layer, and its contract-check step fails closed when the workflow drifts from these values. Only the dedicated conformance workflow is in this campaign's semantic closure, so unrelated quality or build changes in ci.yml do not invalidate retained conformance evidence.
identity_note: workflow_git_blob and script_git_blob are the fail-closed authority, not the literal/semantic fields below them. They are each file's exact `git hash-object` identity: any byte-level change to the workflow or the script — an added trigger, a job-level permission override, a widened matrix, a changed command, an appended line — moves the identity and fails the contract check, whether or not every literal field below still happens to read true. The literal fields exist for a readable diagnostic, not as the boundary. This document does not hash itself: that would be self-referential, since updating the identities to match a legitimate change would also change the file recording them.
matrix_note: The two ends of the supported PostgreSQL 15-18 range. Evidence is required from both, exactly once each.
profile_note: Debug, like every M5 campaign except performance, whose denominator requires release for figures comparable to release planning. The conformance campaign gates correctness — every accepted row's scenarios ran and passed, on both PostgreSQL majors — not a duration, so nothing here depends on the profile.
features: the workspace test suite the campaign runs is built and run with --all-features by cargo xtask conformance's own target invocations
artifact_retention: on success and on failure alike, because what a failed conformance campaign is mostly worth reading for is which accepted row, or which unrelated target, it lost
timeout_note: The campaign runs every workspace test target cargo metadata reports (66 at the time this contract was written) plus the workspace documentation tests, not one bounded workload, so its ceiling is the widest of the M5 campaigns. Still a ceiling: a campaign that stopped making progress must fail rather than occupy a runner.
